title: Projective constructibility from projective-line constructibility
statement:
Suppose $\mathcal C(\mathbf P^1_T\to T)$ holds for every
finite-type $k$-scheme $T$. Then $\mathcal C(f)$ holds for
every projective morphism $f:X\to S$ between finite-type
$k$-schemes, using the conventions of
[def-finrepair-property-c], [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions].
Here projective has the closed-embedding convention of [def-pc-projective-morphism].

proof.text: Let $f:X\to S$ be as in the statement. By [def-pc-projective-morphism], choose an integer $n\geq0$ and a closed immersion $i:X\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^n_S$ with $f=p_n i$. This convention supplies a global embedding.

source.place: ## Proof, first paragraph: choosing the projective embedding

proof.text: Use the equality of the base-change and relative-Proj presentations in [def-nagata-projective-space-base-change]. Over an affine open $\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq S$, the standard opens in [def-nagata-relative-projective-space] are the degree-zero localizations of $A[T_0,\ldots,T_r]$ at $T_i$. These are $A[T_j/T_i:j\ne i]$: a homogeneous numerator of degree $d$ divided by $T_i^d$ is a polynomial in the ratios, and substitution of these ratios gives the inverse homomorphism. Thus a finite affine cover of $S$ by finitely generated $k$-algebras gives a finite affine cover of $\mathbf P^r_S$ by finitely generated $k$-algebras, since adjoining the ratios to generators of $A$ generates each chart. This is finite type by [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Define $Z_0=S$ and recursively $Z_{m+1}=\mathbf P^1_{Z_m}$ with its projection to $Z_m$. The same two-chart calculation at each stage proves by induction that every $Z_m$ is finite type over $k$. These recursive schemes are the products $(\mathbf P^1_S)^m$ over $S$: by [def-pc-fibre-product] and the base-change presentation, a map to $\mathbf P^1_{Z_m}=Z_m\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z}\mathbf P^1_{\mathbf Z}$ is exactly a map to $Z_m$ and a map to $\mathbf P^1_{\mathbf Z}$ with equal composites to $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$. Equivalently it is a map to $Z_m$ and a map to $\mathbf P^1_S$ with equal composites to $S$. The two universal properties give inverse morphisms $\mathbf P^1_{Z_m}\simeq Z_m\times_S\mathbf P^1_S$, commuting with the projections; iterating gives the claimed product identification.

The field $k$ is Noetherian, since its only ideals are $0$ and $k$, and $\operatorname{Spec}k$ is quasi-compact and locally Noetherian. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] to $S\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ to conclude that $S$ is Noetherian. This verifies the base hypothesis for [lem-fin-symmetric-product-finite].

We prove $\mathcal C(Z_m\to S)$ by induction on $m$. For $m=0$ this is the identity: its direct image is the identity exact functor, so its positive right-derived functors vanish and its degree-zero direct image preserves constructibility, as required by [def-finrepair-property-c]. The zero sheaf is finite constant (with value the zero $\Lambda$-module), hence constructible by [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes]. The projection $Z_{m+1}=\mathbf P^1_{Z_m}\to Z_m$ satisfies $\mathcal C$ by the hypothesis, since $Z_m$ is finite type over $k$. The inductive hypothesis and [lem-finrepair-composition-c] give $\mathcal C(Z_{m+1}\to S)$. This proves the induction for all $m$.

If $n\geq1$, [lem-fin-symmetric-product-finite] supplies a finite surjective map $\sigma_n:Z_n\to\mathbf P^n_S$ over the Noetherian base $S$. Its composite with $p_n$ is the product projection $Z_n\to S$, which satisfies $\mathcal C$ by the preceding induction. Both $\mathbf P^n_S$ and $Z_n$ are finite type over $k$. Hence [lem-finrepair-finite-surjection-cancellation], applied to $f=p_n$ and $\pi=\sigma_n$, proves $\mathcal C(p_n)$. If $n=0$, the single standard chart identifies $\mathbf P^0_S$ with $S$, so $p_0$ is the identity and the base-case argument applies.

For every constructible $\Lambda$-sheaf $G$ on $X$, [lem-fin-closed-immersion] says that $i_*G$ is constructible and $R^qi_*G=0$ for $q>0$. Its target $\mathbf P^n_S$ is finite type over $k$, as checked above, so the cited lemma applies. The zero sheaf is finite constant with value the zero $\Lambda$-module, hence constructible by [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes]. Thus $\mathcal C(i)$ holds by [def-finrepair-property-c]. Combine $\mathcal C(i)$ with $\mathcal C(p_n)$ using [lem-finrepair-composition-c] to obtain $\mathcal C(f)$.
